messages:
maria: Hi folks — opening a small docs PR to add a reproducible snippet and troubleshooting checklist for streaming -> batch fallback when clients hit repeated 429s during long responses. Draft PR: #4980

liam: nice, link? want to keep examples compact for node/python/ruby if possible.

maria: link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4980 (WIP). Node and Python snippets in the draft, ruby optional. Core idea: attempt streaming; on >2 429s within short window, fall back to a single-request non-streaming mode with exponential backoff + jitter.

sam: please capture edge cases: Reply to 429s with Retry-After header, differentiate transient 429s vs sustained pool saturation (Dedicated). Also mention trimming tokens or switching to a smaller model before retrying.

maria: added a short paragraph about Dedicated vs Private: Dedicated tends to show pool-saturation 429s; Private installs may return 429s from local rate-limiting proxies — operator config note added.

jen: QA offer: I can run the dev-sim and attach output. Can you add exact curl commands and a tiny harness (node) that logs the sequence? makes testing faster.

maria: added a test harness and a curl sim step: 

```bash
# spin up dev-sim to return controlled 429 bursts
curl -X POST "https://dev-sim.redwood.internal/simulate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"scenario":"burst-429","path":"/v1/chat/completions"}'
```

and a minimal node harness in the snippet: 
```js
// attempt streaming, fallback to single request on repeated 429s
let retries = 0
while (retries < 4) {
  const res = await client.streamCreate(payload)
  if (res.ok) break
  if (res.status === 429) {
    retries++
    await sleep(expBackoff(retries) + jitter())
    if (retries >= 2) {
      // switch to non-streaming path
      const batch = await client.create(payloadNonStreaming)
      return batch
    }
  } else { throw new Error('unexpected') }
}
```

liam: good. Add a short "expected signals" list and a one-line remediation matrix: 429 -> backoff + batch; 408 -> increase client timeout; 413/409 -> trim context; 500/503 -> retry with capped attempts.

maria: added matrix with one-line remediation bullets. Also added a tiny escalation section: when to ping eng-runtime (e.g., consistent >1% 429s across traffic, mismatched per-route latency spikes).

sam: please ensure cross-links to err-ref entries for 429s/timeouts/context limits. Also add a note about SDKs: our unified SDK returns a typed error object with .code === 'RateLimited' for easier handling — show that in examples.

maria: included SDK error example and updated the Python snippet to check for error.code.

docs-bot: PR created by maria: #4980 — reviewers requested: @liam @sam :eyes:

liam: I'll take a pass tonight and try to port ruby if time. If QA passes on dev-sim, we can land this as a small docs patch.

jen: I'll post the sim output once I run it. Planning to validate both stream resume behavior and the batch fallback correctness.

sam: tiny nit: spell out the guidance for jitter (eg. full jitter) and include a reference to our backoff util in the SDK repo.

maria: done. thanks all — will ping when I push the updated patch with python fixes and QA notes.
